audits.mathematicalReason: For z = x + iy, the product is (3x − 4y) + i(4x + 3y). It is real exactly when 4x + 3y = 0, a line through the origin. Alternatively, writing the real product as t gives z = t/(3 + 4i) = t(3 − 4i)/25 for every real t. These are all real scalar multiples of one nonzero direction, including the origin when t = 0. Both proposed routes correctly identify the complex-plane locus.

Using S_m = ma + m(m−1)d/2 gives R = S_(3n) − S_(2n) − S_n = 2n²d. The coefficient of a cancels, so the expression depends on d and n, not a. The alternative pairing method also works: S_(3n) − S_(2n) is the sum of terms a_(2n+k), for k = 1,...,n, and each difference a_(2n+k) − a_k equals 2nd. Their sum is 2n²d. The sum formula is a defensible selected method, not a universally necessary one.

When the kth line is added, it meets the preceding k−1 lines at distinct points because there are no parallel pairs or concurrent triples. These points divide it into k pieces, each splitting one existing region and creating one new region. Hence R_k = R_(k−1) + k with R_0 = 1. Therefore R_6 = 1 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 22. The general-position assumptions justify using the line count as the recurrence state.

For side length s > 0, the square's diagonal has length √(s² + s²) = s√2. If h is the triangle's altitude to that diagonal, equality of areas gives (s√2)h/2 = s², so h = s√2. The scalene condition does not alter the base-height area relation, and the altitude's foot need not lie within the base segment. The proposed Pythagorean and triangle-area scopes directly support this solution.

The light is not green for 5 + 30 = 35 seconds of every 60-second cycle, giving probability 35/60 = 7/12 under uniform phase sampling. Equivalently, the cycle can be partitioned into twelve equally likely five-second intervals, seven of which are yellow or red. This finite equally likely model supports the proposed scope.
limitations: Interprets a randomly chosen time as a uniform phase within the cycle; switching instants have probability zero.

Because RS does not intersect the triangle, all three vertices lie in the same open half-plane; orient coordinates so their y-coordinates are 10,6,24. The centroid's perpendicular coordinate is their mean, so GH = (10 + 6 + 24)/3 = 40/3. This follows directly from the 2:1 median ratio: the midpoint of BC has y-coordinate 15, and G lies two-thirds of the way from A to that midpoint, giving 10 + (2/3)(15 − 10) = 40/3.
